title: Base change between small etale sites is continuous; direct image preserves sheaves of sets
statement: Let $u:U\to V$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $V_{\Et}$, $U_{\Et}$ the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and $b:V_{\Et}\to U_{\Et}$, $W\mapsto U\times_VW$, $(g:W_1\to W_2)\mapsto\mathrm{id}_U\times g$, the base-change functor. Then: (1) $b$ sends coverings to coverings: if $\{W_i\to W\}_{i}$ is a covering of $V_{\Et}$ (etale morphisms over $V$, jointly surjective), then $\{U\times_VW_i\to U\times_VW\}_i$ is a covering of $U_{\Et}$; (2) for a morphism $W'\to W$ and a morphism $W''\to W$ of $V_{\Et}$ the canonical map $U\times_V(W'\times_WW'')\to(U\times_VW')\times_{U\times_VW}(U\times_VW'')$ is an isomorphism; (3) consequently $b$ is a continuous functor of sites (Stacks, Sites, Definition 00WV), and for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ on $U_{\Et}$ the presheaf $u_*\mathcal F=\mathcal F\circ b$, $W\mapsto\mathcal F(U\times_VW)$, is a sheaf of sets on $V_{\Et}$; the sheaf condition of $u_*\mathcal F$ for a covering $\{W_i\to W\}$ is the sheaf condition of $\mathcal F$ for the covering $\{U\times_VW_i\to U\times_VW\}$. The same holds for sheaves of abelian groups and of commutative rings, whose sheaf condition is that of the underlying presheaf of sets.

source.place: Definition 00WV (definition-continuous: u continuous if it sends coverings to coverings and commutes with the fibre products of coverings) and Lemma 00WW (lemma-pushforward-sheaf: u^p of a sheaf is a sheaf for a continuous u, the sheaf conditions being the same); base change of etale coverings: literature/stacks-project/topologies.tex Lemma 0217 (lemma-etale: an etale covering base-changes to an etale covering) with Definition 0215 (definition-etale-covering) and Definition 021B (the small etale site)

proof.text: *Step 1 (b is a well-defined functor; clause (2)).* By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] (1), for an object $W\to V$ of $V_{\Et}$ the base change $U\times_VW\to U$ is etale, and $W\mapsto U\times_VW$, $(g:W_1\to W_2)\mapsto\mathrm{id}_U\times g$ is a functor $b:V_{\Et}\to U_{\Et}$. By (2) of the same node, $W'\times_WW''$ (scheme-theoretic fibre product with its map to $V$) is the fibre product in $V_{\Et}$, and by (3) the canonical morphism $U\times_V(W'\times_WW'')\to(U\times_VW')\times_{U\times_VW}(U\times_VW'')$, i.e. the morphism $(b(\mathrm{pr}_1),b(\mathrm{pr}_2))$ given by the universal property of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], is an isomorphism; it is compatible with the projections: its composites with the two projections are $b(\mathrm{pr}_1)$ and $b(\mathrm{pr}_2)$. This is clause (2).

source.place: Definition 00WV, condition (2) (u(T x_V V_i) -> u(T) x_{u(V)} u(V_i) an isomorphism); the fibre products of the small etale site: literature/stacks-project/topologies.tex Definition 021B (definition-big-small-etale)

proof.text: *Step 2 (clause (1): b sends coverings to coverings).* Let $\{g_i:W_i\to W\}_{i\in I}$ be a covering of $V_{\Et}$: by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms. Write $h:W\to V$ for the structure morphism, $p:U\times_VW\to W$ and $q:U\times_VW\to U$ for the projections, and $p_i:U\times_VW_i\to W_i$, $q_i:U\times_VW_i\to U$. Consider the diagram with rows $U\times_VW_i\xrightarrow{p_i}W_i$, $U\times_VW\xrightarrow{p}W$, $U\xrightarrow{u}V$ and columns $\mathrm{id}_U\times g_i:U\times_VW_i\to U\times_VW$, $g_i$, then $q$, $h$. It commutes ($g_ip_i=p(\mathrm{id}_U\times g_i)$ and $hp=uq$ by the definition of $\mathrm{id}_U\times g_i$ through the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]). The lower square is cartesian ($U\times_VW$ is the fibre product of $u$ and $h$), and the outer rectangle is cartesian: $(U\times_VW_i,p_i,q\circ(\mathrm{id}_U\times g_i)=q_i)$ is the fibre product of $u$ and $h g_i$, the structure morphism of $W_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] the upper square is cartesian: $(U\times_VW_i,\ \mathrm{id}_U\times g_i,\ p_i)$ is a fibre product of $p$ and $g_i$, so there is an isomorphism $\theta_i:U\times_VW_i\xrightarrow{\sim}(U\times_VW)\times_WW_i$ with $k_i\circ\theta_i=\mathrm{id}_U\times g_i$, $k_i$ the first projection. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change], applied to the jointly surjective etale family $\{g_i\}$ and the morphism $p:U\times_VW\to W$, the projections $k_i:(U\times_VW)\times_WW_i\to U\times_VW$ are etale and jointly surjective. Hence $\mathrm{id}_U\times g_i=k_i\theta_i$ is etale (an isomorphism is an open immersion, hence etale, and a composite of etale morphisms is etale, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1), (2)), and its image equals the image of $k_i$ since $\theta_i$ is bijective; so $\bigcup_i\mathrm{im}(\mathrm{id}_U\times g_i)=\bigcup_i\mathrm{im}(k_i)=U\times_VW$. Thus $\{b(W_i)\to b(W)\}_i$ is a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms between objects of $U_{\Et}$, i.e. a covering of $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site].

source.place: Lemma 0217 (lemma-etale) (3): base change of an etale covering is an etale covering, with Definition 0215 (definition-etale-covering) and Definition 021B; the identification U x_V W_i = (U x_V W) x_W W_i is the pasting of cartesian squares

proof.text: *Step 3 (b is continuous).* Stacks' Definition 00WV asks, for every covering $\{W_i\to W\}$ of $V_{\Et}$: (a) $\{b(W_i)\to b(W)\}$ is a covering of $U_{\Et}$, which is step 2; (b) for every morphism $T\to W$ of $V_{\Et}$ the canonical morphism $b(T\times_WW_i)\to b(T)\times_{b(W)}b(W_i)$ is an isomorphism, which is step 1 (clause (2)) with $W'=T$, $W''=W_i$. So $b$ is continuous; this is the first part of clause (3).

*Step 4 (u_* F = F o b is a sheaf; the two sheaf conditions are the same).* Let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of sets on $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] and $\{g_i:W_i\to W\}$ a covering of $V_{\Et}$. The sheaf condition of $\mathcal F\circ b$ for it is that $\mathcal F(bW)\to\prod_i\mathcal F(bW_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\mathcal F(b(W_i\times_WW_j))$, with maps $\mathcal F(b g_i)$ and $\mathcal F(b\,\mathrm{pr}_1)$, $\mathcal F(b\,\mathrm{pr}_2)$, is an equalizer. By step 1 the canonical $\varphi_{ij}:b(W_i\times_WW_j)\to bW_i\times_{bW}bW_j$ is an isomorphism with $\mathrm{pr}_1\varphi_{ij}=b(\mathrm{pr}_1)$, $\mathrm{pr}_2\varphi_{ij}=b(\mathrm{pr}_2)$; so $\prod_{i,j}\mathcal F(\varphi_{ij})$ is a bijection $\prod_{i,j}\mathcal F(bW_i\times_{bW}bW_j)\to\prod_{i,j}\mathcal F(b(W_i\times_WW_j))$ which carries the two maps of the diagram of $\mathcal F$ for the family $\{b g_i:bW_i\to bW\}$ to the two maps above (functoriality of $\mathcal F$), and the first maps agree. Hence the diagram for $\mathcal F\circ b$ and $\{W_i\to W\}$ is isomorphic, by the identity on the first two terms and a bijection on the third, to the diagram of $\mathcal F$ for $\{bW_i\to bW\}$; the latter family is a covering of $U_{\Et}$ by step 2, so that diagram is an equalizer since $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf; an equalizer property only depends on the diagram up to such an isomorphism (the equalizer of two maps is unchanged by composing both with the same injection), so the diagram of $\mathcal F\circ b$ is an equalizer. Thus $u_*\mathcal F=\mathcal F\circ b$ is a sheaf of sets on $V_{\Et}$, and $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F\circ b$, $\varphi\mapsto\varphi\circ b$ (whiskering) is a functor $\Sh(U_{\Et})\to\Sh(V_{\Et})$. If $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of abelian groups (resp. commutative rings), $\mathcal F\circ b$ is a presheaf of abelian groups (rings) with the same sections and restriction maps, and its sheaf condition is the equalizer condition of the underlying presheaf of sets [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] (the equalizer in sets of homomorphisms carries the induced structure), so the same argument shows $\mathcal F\circ b$ is a sheaf of abelian groups (rings).

source.place: Lemma 00WW (lemma-pushforward-sheaf) and its proof: 'the sheaf condition for u^p F and the covering {V_i -> V} is precisely the same as the sheaf condition for F and the covering {u(V_i) -> u(V)}'
